claims.claim: No major FRET changes were observed when RSC was added to the nucleosomes in the absence of ATP.
claims.source: As expected, no major FRET changes were observed when RSC was added to the nucleosomes in the absence of ATP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The ATPase of RSC is incapable of translocating past a 2-nt single-stranded gap in the DNA.
claims.source: In order to confirm our assignment of entry-side and exit-side movement traces, we made use of the fact that the ATPase of RSC is incapable of translocating past a 2-nt single-stranded (ss) gap in the DNA (Saha et al., 2005; Zofall et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claims.claim: Remodeling of a construct containing a gap at the SHL–2 site showed only a single peak at zero FRET after remodeling.
claims.source: As expected, remodeling of a construct containing a gap at the SHL–2 site showed only a single peak at zero FRET after remodeling (Figure 1F), consistent with the gap preventing RSC from engaging the SHL–2 site to generate entry-side movement traces.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: >95% of the remodeling traces from the construct with a gap at the SHL–2 site were classified as exit-side movement traces and showed a monotonic FRET decrease without an initial FRET increase.
claims.source: Furthermore, >95% of the remodeling traces from this construct were classified as exit-side movement traces and showed a monotonic FRET decrease without an initial FRET increase (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A,B.

claims.claim: A gap at the SHL+2 site largely eliminated the zero FRET population and resulted in essentially a single population with a FRET of ~0.14 after remodeling.
claims.source: Similarly, a gap at the SHL+2 site largely eliminated the zero FRET population and resulted in essentially a single population with a FRET of ~0.14 after remodeling (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Only a small fraction (~8%) of nucleosomes with a gap at the SHL+2 site showed a final FRET of zero, which is most likely due to photobleaching of the Cy5 dye during remodeling.
claims.source: Only a small fraction (~8%) of nucleosomes showed a final FRET of zero, which is most likely due to photobleaching of the Cy5 dye during remodeling.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claims.claim: >95% of the traces observed from the construct with a gap at the SHL+2 site were classified as entry-side movement traces and showed an initial FRET increase during remodeling.
claims.source: Moreover, >95% of the traces observed were classified as entry-side movement traces and showed an initial FRET increase during remodeling (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C,D), consistent with the gap preventing RSC from engaging the SHL+2 site and generating exit-side movement traces.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C,D.

claims.claim: After incubating the H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes with 5 nM RSC and 5 µM ATP for 20 min, >90% of the nucleosomes remained present with the H2A subunit attached.
claims.source: Indeed, after incubating the H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes with 5 nM RSC and 5 µM ATP for 20 min, >90% of the nucleosomes remained present with the H2A subunit attached, similar to the fraction of nucleosomes remaining intact after incubation in the absence of RSC and ATP (91%).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental measurements.

claims.claim: Remodeling of the H3-labeled nucleosomes produced two classes of FRET traces, one class showing a monotonic decrease in FRET and the other class showing an initial FRET increase followed by a FRET decrease.
claims.source: Similar to H2A-labeled nucleosomes, remodeling of the H3-labeled nucleosomes also produced two classes of FRET traces, one class showing a monotonic decrease in FRET (Figure 2B) and the other class showing an initial FRET increase followed by a FRET decrease (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claims.claim: Placing a gap at the SHL–2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated nearly all of the traces showing an initial FRET increase.
claims.source: As in the case of the H2A/[end,+6] constructs, placing a gap at the SHL–2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated nearly all of the traces showing an initial FRET increase, and placing a gap at the SHL+2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated most of the traces showing a monotonic FRET decrease (Figure 2D), indicating that these traces reflect entry-side and exit-side movement, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Placing a gap at the SHL+2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated most of the traces showing a monotonic FRET decrease.
claims.source: As in the case of the H2A/[end,+6] constructs, placing a gap at the SHL–2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated nearly all of the traces showing an initial FRET increase, and placing a gap at the SHL+2 site of the H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes eliminated most of the traces showing a monotonic FRET decrease (Figure 2D), indicating that these traces reflect entry-side and exit-side movement, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The observation that the FRET changes were similar for the H2A-labeled and H3-labeled nucleosomes suggests that these observed FRET changes were not specific to the dynamics of the H2A-H2B dimer.
claims.source: The observation that the FRET changes were similar for the H2A-labeled and H3-labeled nucleosomes suggests that these observed FRET changes were not specific to the dynamics of the H2A-H2B dimer.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data comparing H2A-labeled and H3-labeled nucleosomes.

claims.claim: Addition of RSC and ATP to the H2A/H2A construct resulted in only a small decrease in FRET, ΔFRET ~0.1.
claims.source: Addition of RSC and ATP to this H2A/H2A construct resulted in only a small decrease in FRET, ΔFRET ~0.1 (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The FRET decrease in the H2A/H2A construct was partially recapitulated by the addition of enzyme in the absence of ATP.
claims.source: This FRET decrease was partially recapitulated by the addition of enzyme in the absence of ATP (Figure 2F), suggesting that this FRET change was associated, at least in part, with RSC binding.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: The apparent FRET change in the H2A/H2A construct was due almost entirely to an increase in Cy3 fluorescence without a corresponding decrease in Cy5 fluorescence.
claims.source: Furthermore, this apparent FRET change was due almost entirely to an increase in Cy3 fluorescence without a corresponding decrease in Cy5 fluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B), suggesting that this apparent FRET change was probably due to a change in the photophysical properties of the Cy3 dye upon RSC binding rather than a bona fide change in distance between the dyes.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: The FRET values of H2B/H2B nucleosomes did not change appreciably after addition of RSC and ATP.
claims.source: The FRET values of these H2B/H2B nucleosomes did not change appreciably after addition of RSC and ATP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Upon addition of RSC and ATP to the H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes, both exit-side and entry-side movement traces were observed.
claims.source: Upon addition of RSC and ATP to the H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes, we again observed both exit-side and entry-side movement traces (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C,D) resembling those obtained with the H2A- and H3-labeled nucleosomes.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C,D.

claims.claim: The H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes showed a preference for entry-side remodeling.
claims.source: The H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes showed a preference for entry-side remodeling (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), perhaps because the label biased binding of RSC in the orientation supporting entry-side remodeling.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: Control constructs with gaps at the SHL–2 or SHL+2 site eliminated nearly all of the entry-side or exit-side movement traces, respectively, for the H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes.
claims.source: However, control constructs with gaps at the SHL–2 or SHL+2 site eliminated nearly all of the entry-side or exit-side movement traces, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), confirming our assignment of entry-side and exit-side movement traces.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: The FRET dynamics observed were due primarily to movement of the DNA relative to the octamer.
claims.source: Thus, in our assays using nucleosomes labeled with Cy3 on the octamer and Cy5 on the DNA, we saw similar entry-side and exit-side movement traces when using three different positions of the Cy3 on the octamer (on H2A, H3 or H2B), suggesting that the FRET dynamics we observed were due primarily to movement of the DNA relative to the octamer.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data from multiple labeling schemes.

claims.claim: When both Cy3 and Cy5 dyes were placed on the H2A-H2B dimer, no substantial motion of the H2A-H2B dimer was observed with two different positions of the dye (on H2A or H2B).
claims.source: Furthermore, when we placed both Cy3 and Cy5 dyes on the H2A-H2B dimer, we did not observe substantial motion of the H2A-H2B dimer with two different positions of the dye (on H2A or H2B).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data from H2A/H2A and H2B/H2B constructs.

claims.claim: The entry-side movement traces showed a substantial increase in FRET followed by a FRET decrease for both H2A/[end, +6] and H3/[end, +6] constructs.
claims.source: The entry-side movement traces that we observed showed a substantial increase in FRET followed by a FRET decrease for both H2A/[end, +6] and H3/[end, +6] constructs (Figures 1C, 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), which was consistent with movement largely along or near the canonical path at the nucleosome edge where DNA enters the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figures 1C, 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The entry-side movement traces were consistent with movement largely along or near the canonical path at the nucleosome edge where DNA enters the nucleosome.
claims.source: The entry-side movement traces that we observed showed a substantial increase in FRET followed by a FRET decrease for both H2A/[end, +6] and H3/[end, +6] constructs (Figures 1C, 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), which was consistent with movement largely along or near the canonical path at the nucleosome edge where DNA enters the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figures 1C, 2C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Similar entry-side movement traces were observed for constructs with increased linker DNA length, such as the H2A/[end,+11] and H3/[end,+9] constructs.
claims.source: This phenomenon was also seen for constructs with increased linker DNA length, such as the H2A/[end,+11] and H3/[end,+9] constructs, where the Cy5 dye-labeled DNA end was initially 11 bp and 9 bp away from the nucleosome edge (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claims.claim: Some entry-side movement traces showed a small apparent decrease in FRET (ΔFRET ~ 0.1) prior to the FRET increase, but this apparent FRET decrease resulted primarily from an increase in Cy3 intensity without a corresponding decrease in Cy5 intensity.
claims.source: Some of these entry-side movement traces also showed a small apparent decrease in FRET (ΔFRET ~ 0.1) prior to the FRET increase, but this apparent FRET decrease resulted primarily from an increase in Cy3 intensity without a corresponding decrease in Cy5 intensity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-F).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-F.

claims.claim: The magnitude of the Cy3 intensity change in entry-side movement traces was consistent with the changes seen when the two H2A subunits on the octamer were labeled with Cy3 and Cy5.
claims.source: The magnitude of this Cy3 intensity change was consistent with the changes seen when we labeled the two H2A subunits on the octamer with Cy3 and Cy5 (i.e. the H2A/H2A construct) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that this FRET change likely resulted from a change in the photophysical properties of the Cy3 dye upon RSC binding.
claims.evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: The small initial FRET decreases observed in entry-side movement traces would correspond to a change in the Cy3-Cy5 distance of only ~0.5 nm.
claims.source: Assuming a previously measured Förster radius of 6 nm for the Cy3-Cy5 pair (Murphy et al., 2004), these small initial FRET decreases that we observed would correspond to a change in the Cy3-Cy5 distance of only ~0.5 nm.
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured FRET changes and the known Förster radius.

claims.claim: Under the remodeling conditions used, the DNA was not lifted by a large distance away from the nucleosomal surface and did not deviate substantially from its canonical wrapping path as it entered the nucleosome.
claims.source: Thus, our data suggest that under our remodeling conditions, the DNA was not lifted by a large distance away from the nucleosomal surface and did not deviate substantially from its canonical wrapping path as it entered the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on entry-side movement.

claims.claim: Addition of RSC and ATP to the H2A/[backbone, –15] construct generated two classes of traces: exit-side movement traces showing a transient increase in FRET followed by a decrease to zero FRET and entry-side movement traces showing a decrease in FRET to ~0.23.
claims.source: Addition of RSC and ATP to this construct again generated two classes of traces: exit-side movement traces showing a transient increase in FRET followed by a decrease to zero FRET (Figure 3B) and entry-side movement traces showing a decrease in FRET to ~0.23 (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claims.claim: Without any ssDNA gap on the H2A/[backbone, –15] nucleosome, the FRET traces preferentially showed entry-side movement.
claims.source: Without any ssDNA gap on the nucleosome, the FRET traces of the H2A/[backbone, –15] construct preferentially showed entry-side movement (Figure 3D), likely because placing the Cy5 inside the nucleosome biased RSC to bind in the orientation that positioned the ATPase at the SHL–2 site.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: When a 2-nt ssDNA gap was introduced at the SHL–2 site of the H2A/[backbone, –15] construct, nearly all of the traces showed the exit-side movement behavior, displaying an initial increase in FRET followed by the decrease to zero FRET.
claims.source: Nevertheless, when we introduced a 2-nt ssDNA gap at the SHL–2 site, nearly all of the traces showed the exit-side movement behavior, displaying an initial increase in FRET followed the decrease to zero FRET; when a 2-nt ssDNA gap was introduced at the SHL+2 site, nearly all of the traces showed the entry-side movement behavior, displaying only a monotonic decrease in FRET (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: When a 2-nt ssDNA gap was introduced at the SHL+2 site of the H2A/[backbone, –15] construct, nearly all of the traces showed the entry-side movement behavior, displaying only a monotonic decrease in FRET.
claims.source: Nevertheless, when we introduced a 2-nt ssDNA gap at the SHL–2 site, nearly all of the traces showed the exit-side movement behavior, displaying an initial increase in FRET followed the decrease to zero FRET; when a 2-nt ssDNA gap was introduced at the SHL+2 site, nearly all of the traces showed the entry-side movement behavior, displaying only a monotonic decrease in FRET (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: The DNA was not lifted away from the nucleosome surface by a large distance and did not deviate substantially from its canonical path as it exited the nucleosome.
claims.source: Because lifting of the DNA by a large distance away from the nucleosomal surface would have caused a FRET decrease instead of an initial FRET increase, our data suggest that the DNA was not lifted away from the nucleosome surface by a large distance and did not deviate substantially from its canonical path as it exited the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data from the H2A/[backbone, –15] construct.

claims.claim: The exit-side movement traces exhibited intermittent pauses interrupting the monotonic decrease to zero FRET.
claims.source: The exit-side movement traces exhibited intermittent pauses interrupting the monotonic decrease to zero FRET (Figure 4A), and we applied a step-finding algorithm based on chi-square minimization (Kerssemakers et al., 2006) to identify the location of the pauses and the sizes of the steps.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: The step size histogram for exit-side movement of H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes showed a distribution of step sizes with a major peak centered at a ΔFRET of 0.1 and a tail extending to larger ΔFRET values.
claims.source: The step size histogram showed a distribution of step sizes with a major peak centered at a ΔFRET of 0.1 and a tail extending to larger ΔFRET values (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the step-finding analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Using an alternative, hidden Markov model (HMM)-based algorithm, similar steps in the FRET traces were identified and a similar step size histogram was produced, again with the major peak centered at a ΔFRET of 0.1.
claims.source: Using an alternative, hidden Markov model (HMM)-based algorithm (McKinney et al., 2006), we identified similar steps in the FRET traces and produced a similar step size histogram, again with the major peak centered at a ΔFRET of 0.1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the alternative step-finding analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: During remodeling of the H2A/[backbone,–15] construct, the vast majority (85%) of the exit-side movement traces showed gradual FRET changes inconsistent with large step sizes.
claims.source: However, during remodeling of the H2A/[backbone,–15] construct (Figure 3), where exit-side movement led to an increase in FRET that can be distinguished from Cy5 photobleaching, the vast majority (85%) of the exit-side movement traces showed gradual FRET changes inconsistent with such large step sizes, suggesting that at most a small fraction of nucleosomes could remodel with such large-step movement.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments on the H2A/[backbone,–15] construct.

claims.claim: The major step size of DNA movement for exit-side movement of H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes, corresponding to the peak of the ΔFRET distribution, was determined to be ~2 bp.
claims.source: From these slopes, we determined that the major step size of DNA movement, corresponding to the peak of the ΔFRET distribution in Figure 4B (ΔFRET ~ 0.1), to be ~2 bp.
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured ΔFRET values and the calibration curves.

claims.claim: The data for exit-side movement of H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes at 2 µM ATP are consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.104 ± 0.002 with a probability of missing a step being f = 34%.
claims.source: The data derived from the step-finding algorithm based on chi-square minimization are consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.104 ± 0.002 with a probability of missing a step being f = 34% (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model.

claims.claim: Analyzing the step size distribution generated from the alternative HMM-based step-finding algorithm produced a step size of ΔFRET of 0.102 ± 0.003 with a missed fraction of f = 41%.
claims.source: Analyzing the step size distribution generated from the alternative HMM-based step-finding algorithm produced a step size of ΔFRET of 0.102 ± 0.003 with a missed fraction of f = 41% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model using an alternative algorithm.

claims.claim: Based on the distribution of observed pause durations, a 25% probability of missing a step due to limited time resolution would be expected.
claims.source: Based on the distribution of observed pause durations, we would expect a 25% probability of missing a step due to our limited time resolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed pause duration distributions shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: The step size distributions for exit-side movement at 20 µM ATP are consistent with a step size of 1.7 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 26%.
claims.source: Fitting the resulting step size histograms to multiple Gaussian peaks as described earlier indicated that the distributions are consistent with a step size of 1.7 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 26% for 20 µM ATP and 2.0 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 41% for 80 µM ATP (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model at 20 µM ATP.

claims.claim: The step size distributions for exit-side movement at 80 µM ATP are consistent with a step size of 2.0 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 41%.
claims.source: Fitting the resulting step size histograms to multiple Gaussian peaks as described earlier indicated that the distributions are consistent with a step size of 1.7 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 26% for 20 µM ATP and 2.0 ± 0.2 bp with a missed step probability of f = 41% for 80 µM ATP (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model at 80 µM ATP.

claims.claim: The exit-side movement traces of the H3/[end, +6] construct showed stepwise DNA translocation.
claims.source: The exit-side movement traces of these new constructs also showed stepwise DNA translocation (Figure 4C,E), and the step size distributions (Figure 4D,F) showed a major peak around a ΔFRET of 0.1 with a tail extending to larger values.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The exit-side movement traces of the H2A/[backbone, +6] construct showed stepwise DNA translocation.
claims.source: The exit-side movement traces of these new constructs also showed stepwise DNA translocation (Figure 4C,E), and the step size distributions (Figure 4D,F) showed a major peak around a ΔFRET of 0.1 with a tail extending to larger values.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: The step size distributions for exit-side movement of H3/[end, +6] nucleosomes were consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.113 ± 0.003 with a missed step probability of f = 34%.
claims.source: Fitting these histograms to multiple Gaussian peaks as described earlier indicated that the distributions were consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.113 ± 0.003 with a missed step probability of f = 34% for H3/[end, +6] and ΔFRET = 0.092 ± 0.004 and f = 42% for H2A/[backbone,+6] (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,C).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model.

claims.claim: The step size distributions for exit-side movement of H2A/[backbone,+6] nucleosomes were consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.092 ± 0.004 and f = 42%.
claims.source: Fitting these histograms to multiple Gaussian peaks as described earlier indicated that the distributions were consistent with a step size of ΔFRET = 0.113 ± 0.003 with a missed step probability of f = 34% for H3/[end, +6] and ΔFRET = 0.092 ± 0.004 and f = 42% for H2A/[backbone,+6] (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,C).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model.

claims.claim: Comparing the ΔFRET values to the slopes of the calibration curves gave step size estimates of 1.9 ± 0.2 bp for the H3/[end, +6] construct and 1.6 ± 0.1 bp for the H2A/[backbone, +6] construct.
claims.source: Comparing the ΔFRET values to the slopes of the calibration curves gave step size estimates of 1.9 ± 0.2 bp and 1.6 ± 0.1 bp for the H3/[end, +6] and H2A/[backbone, +6] constructs, respectively, consistent with the 2.0 ± 0.2 bp step size estimate for the H2A/[end, +6] construct.
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured ΔFRET values and the calibration curves.

claims.claim: The entry-side movement traces measured at 2 µM ATP primarily showed an increase in FRET as expected from the movement of the short linker DNA into the nucleosome.
claims.source: The entry-side movement traces measured at 2 µM ATP primarily showed an increase in FRET as expected from the movement of the short linker DNA into the nucleosome, bringing the Cy5 dye closer to Cy3.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments.

claims.claim: The FRET increase during entry-side movement occurred in a stepwise manner, indicating stepwise DNA translocation into the nucleosome.
claims.source: The FRET increase occurred in a stepwise manner, indicating stepwise DNA translocation into the nucleosome (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: The distributions of the ΔFRET step sizes for entry-side movement again showed a major peak around ~0.1 with a tail extending to larger values.
claims.source: The distributions of the ΔFRET step sizes again showed a major peak around ~0.1 with a tail extending to larger values (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the step-finding analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claims.claim: Fitting the step size distributions for entry-side movement to multiple evenly spaced Gaussian peaks yielded a step size of ΔFRET = 0.088 ± 0.002 with a missed step probability of f = 22% for the H2A/[end, +12] construct.
claims.source: Fitting to multiple evenly spaced Gaussian peaks as described earlier yielded a step size of ΔFRET = 0.088 ± 0.002 with a missed step probability of f = 22% for the H2A/[end, +12] construct and ΔFRET = 0.084 ± 0.001 and f = 17% for the H3/[end, +9] construct (Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model.

claims.claim: Fitting the step size distributions for entry-side movement to multiple evenly spaced Gaussian peaks yielded a step size of ΔFRET = 0.084 ± 0.001 and f = 17% for the H3/[end, +9] construct.
claims.source: Fitting to multiple evenly spaced Gaussian peaks as described earlier yielded a step size of ΔFRET = 0.088 ± 0.002 with a missed step probability of f = 22% for the H2A/[end, +12] construct and ΔFRET = 0.084 ± 0.001 and f = 17% for the H3/[end, +9] construct (Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distribution to a model.

claims.claim: Based on the calibration curves, the step size distributions for entry-side movement were consistent with step sizes of 1.6 ± 0.1 and 1.7 ± 0.2 bp for the H2A/[end, +12] and H3/[end, +9] constructs, respectively.
claims.source: Based on these slopes, the step size distributions were consistent with step sizes of 1.6 ± 0.1 and 1.7 ± 0.2 bp, respectively, for these constructs.
claims.evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured ΔFRET values and the calibration curves.

claims.claim: The entry-side movement traces from experiments at 20 µM and 80 µM ATP also showed a stepwise increase in FRET.
claims.source: The entry-side movement traces from these experiments also showed a stepwise increase in FRET (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The resulting step size distributions for entry-side movement at 20 µM and 80 µM ATP were consistent with step sizes of 2.0 ± 0.1 bp at 20 µM ATP and 1.9 ± 0.2 bp at 80 µM ATP.
claims.source: The resulting step size distributions were consistent with step sizes of 2.0 ± 0.1 bp at 20 µM ATP and 1.9 ± 0.2 bp at 80 µM ATP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), again similar to the results measured at 2 µM ATP.
claims.evidence: This is a result from fitting the step size distributions to a model at higher ATP concentrations.

claims.claim: Results from experiments using a number of different labeling schemes and ATP concentrations suggested that RSC translocated DNA primarily in ~1–2 bp increments at both the entry side and exit side of the nucleosome.
claims.source: Therefore, our results from experiments using a number of different labeling schemes and ATP concentrations suggested that RSC translocated DNA primarily in ~1–2 bp increments at both the entry side and exit side of the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from multiple labeling schemes and ATP concentrations.

claims.claim: RSC remodeled mononucleosomes primarily by translocating DNA around the nucleosome under the remodeling conditions used (without acceptor nucleosomes, acceptor DNA, transcription factors, chaperones, or other remodeling factors).
claims.source: Our results showed that RSC remodeled mononucleosomes primarily by translocating DNA around the nucleosome under our remodeling conditions (without acceptor nucleosomes, acceptor DNA, transcription factors, chaperones, or other remodeling factors).

results.result: Background on SWI/SNF-family remodelers: These enzymes regulate chromatin structure by coupling ATP hydrolysis to nucleosome repositioning and restructuring. They can reposition octamers, eject H2A-H2B dimers, and eject entire octamers. The catalytic subunit contains an SF2 ATPase domain that contacts nucleosomes at the SHL2 site and translocates DNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C13 establish well-documented background knowledge about SWI/SNF remodelers, all supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These provide essential context for interpreting the current study's findings.

results.result: Prior work on DNA translocation step sizes: The isolated catalytic subunit of SWI/SNF translocates naked DNA in ~2 bp steps, but holoenzyme complexes were reported to move DNA in ~50 bp steps. Related ISWI-family remodelers move DNA in multi-bp compound steps composed of 1-bp fundamental steps. RSC cannot translocate past 2-nt ssDNA gaps.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C19, C21, C24, and C30 accurately summarize prior literature with appropriate citations. These establish the knowledge gap that motivated the current study: whether SWI/SNF remodelers use small or large fundamental step sizes.

results.result: Single-molecule FRET assay development and validation: Mononucleosomes were reconstituted on 601 positioning sequence DNA with FRET dyes on the octamer and DNA. Upon RSC and ATP addition, two classes of traces were observed: exit-side movement (monotonic FRET decrease to zero) and entry-side movement (initial FRET increase then decrease to ~0.17). Roughly equal numbers of each trace type were observed, independent of 601 sequence orientation. Surface attachment did not substantially affect remodeling kinetics compared to ensemble measurements.
results.evaluation: Claims C20, C22-C23, C25-C29 describe the experimental design and initial observations with appropriate controls (no ATP, ensemble comparison, sequence orientation). The data in Figures 1B-D and supplements support bidirectional remodeling and validate the surface-based assay.

results.result: Validation of entry-side and exit-side movement assignments using ssDNA gaps: Placing a 2-nt gap at SHL-2 eliminated entry-side traces (>95% exit-side), showing only zero FRET products. Placing a gap at SHL+2 eliminated exit-side traces (>95% entry-side), showing FRET ~0.14 products. These results confirm that entry-side movement results from ATPase action at SHL-2 and exit-side from action at SHL+2.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C35 describe elegant control experiments using the known inability of RSC to translocate past ssDNA gaps (C30). The data in Figures 1E-G and supplements strongly support the directional assignments, with >95% specificity in both cases.

results.result: H2A-H2B dimer stability during remodeling assessed with H3-labeled nucleosomes: >90% of nucleosomes retained H2A after 20 min remodeling. H3-labeled nucleosomes showed similar FRET dynamics to H2A-labeled nucleosomes, with both exit-side and entry-side movement traces. Gap controls confirmed directional assignments. The similarity of FRET changes suggests they are not specific to H2A-H2B dimer dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C40 are supported by data in Figure 2A-D showing that moving the FRET donor from H2A to H3 produces similar remodeling traces. This argues against major H2A-H2B dimer displacement, though the authors appropriately note that smaller movements cannot be excluded.

results.result: H2A/H2A construct shows minimal FRET change during remodeling: Addition of RSC and ATP to nucleosomes with Cy3 and Cy5 on the two H2A subunits resulted in only a small FRET decrease (ΔFRET ~0.1), partially recapitulated by RSC binding without ATP. This apparent FRET change was due almost entirely to increased Cy3 fluorescence without corresponding Cy5 decrease, suggesting a photophysical artifact rather than true distance change.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C43 are supported by data in Figure 2E-F and supplements. The analysis of individual dye intensities (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) provides strong evidence that the small FRET change is a photophysical artifact from RSC binding rather than H2A-H2B dimer movement.

results.result: H2B-labeled nucleosomes confirm DNA movement without substantial dimer displacement: H2B/H2B nucleosomes showed no appreciable FRET change with RSC and ATP. H2B/[end,+0] nucleosomes showed both entry-side and exit-side movement traces, with gap controls confirming directional assignments. Similar traces with H2A, H3, and H2B labeling suggest FRET dynamics reflect DNA movement relative to the octamer, not H2A-H2B dimer motion.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C49 are supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2. The consistency across three different octamer labeling positions (H2A, H3, H2B) strongly supports the interpretation that FRET changes primarily reflect DNA movement rather than dimer dynamics, though small-scale movements cannot be excluded.

results.result: DNA moves along or near its canonical path at the nucleosome entry site: Entry-side movement traces showed substantial FRET increase followed by decrease for H2A/[end,+6] and H3/[end,+6] constructs, consistent with movement along the canonical path. Similar traces were observed with longer linker DNA. Small initial FRET decreases (ΔFRET ~0.1, corresponding to ~0.5 nm distance change) were observed but attributed to photophysical effects. The data suggest DNA was not lifted by a large distance from the nucleosomal surface as it entered.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C56 are supported by data in Figures 1C, 2C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1. The FRET increase upon entry-side movement is inconsistent with large-scale DNA lifting and supports movement along the canonical path. The photophysical interpretation of small initial FRET decreases is supported by comparison with H2A/H2A controls.

results.result: DNA moves along or near its canonical path at the nucleosome exit site: H2A/[backbone,-15] nucleosomes with Cy5 inside the nucleosome edge showed exit-side traces with transient FRET increase followed by decrease to zero, and entry-side traces with monotonic FRET decrease. Gap controls confirmed directional assignments. The initial FRET increase during exit-side movement indicates DNA was not lifted by a large distance from the nucleosomal surface as it exited.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 are supported by data in Figure 3B-D. The clever placement of Cy5 inside the nucleosome edge allows discrimination between DNA lifting (which would cause FRET decrease) and movement along the canonical path (which causes the observed FRET increase). The data strongly support movement along or near the canonical path.

results.result: Exit-side DNA translocation occurs in ~2 bp steps for H2A/[end,+6] nucleosomes: Exit-side movement traces showed intermittent pauses. Step-finding analysis revealed a step size distribution with a major peak at ΔFRET ~0.1 and a tail to larger values. Two independent algorithms gave consistent results. Calibration curves indicated the major step size corresponds to ~2 bp. Fitting to a model with uniform step size and missed steps gave ΔFRET = 0.104 ± 0.002 with 34% missed steps (chi-square method) or 0.102 ± 0.003 with 41% missed steps (HMM method). The missed step probability is reasonable given the 25% expected from time resolution limitations.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C69 are supported by data in Figure 4A-B and supplements. The use of two independent step-finding algorithms strengthens the conclusions. The calibration approach is sound, and the missed step probability is consistent with experimental limitations. However, the tail to larger step sizes and the observation that some missed step probabilities exceed time resolution limitations (C69) suggest occasional larger steps may occur.

results.result: Exit-side step size is similar at higher ATP concentrations: At 20 µM ATP, step size was 1.7 ± 0.2 bp with 26% missed steps. At 80 µM ATP, step size was 2.0 ± 0.2 bp with 41% missed steps. These are similar to results at 2 µM ATP.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C71 are supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4. The consistency across ATP concentrations strengthens the conclusion that ~1-2 bp is the fundamental step size, though the authors appropriately note that measurements were performed at limiting ATP concentrations (up to Km).

results.result: Exit-side step size is consistent across different labeling schemes: H3/[end,+6] nucleosomes showed stepwise translocation with ΔFRET = 0.113 ± 0.003 (34% missed steps), corresponding to 1.9 ± 0.2 bp. H2A/[backbone,+6] nucleosomes showed ΔFRET = 0.092 ± 0.004 (42% missed steps), corresponding to 1.6 ± 0.1 bp. These are consistent with the 2.0 ± 0.2 bp estimate for H2A/[end,+6].
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C76 are supported by data in Figure 4C-F and supplements. The consistency across three different labeling schemes (different dye positions on both octamer and DNA) strongly supports the conclusion that the observed step sizes reflect true DNA translocation rather than labeling artifacts.

results.result: Entry-side DNA translocation occurs in ~1.6-1.7 bp steps: Entry-side movement traces at 2 µM ATP showed stepwise FRET increase. Step size distributions showed a major peak at ΔFRET ~0.1 with a tail to larger values. For H2A/[end,+12], ΔFRET = 0.088 ± 0.002 with 22% missed steps, corresponding to 1.6 ± 0.1 bp. For H3/[end,+9], ΔFRET = 0.084 ± 0.001 with 17% missed steps, corresponding to 1.7 ± 0.2 bp.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C82 are supported by data in Figure 5A-D and supplements. The entry-side step sizes are similar to exit-side step sizes, supporting a unified mechanism. The lower missed step probabilities for entry-side movement are consistent with the observed pause duration distributions.

results.result: Entry-side step size is similar at higher ATP concentrations: At 20 µM ATP, step size was 2.0 ± 0.1 bp. At 80 µM ATP, step size was 1.9 ± 0.2 bp. These are similar to results at 2 µM ATP.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C84 are supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3. The consistency across ATP concentrations for entry-side movement parallels the exit-side results and strengthens the overall conclusion about fundamental step size.

results.result: Summary of main findings: RSC translocates DNA primarily in ~1-2 bp increments at both entry and exit sides of the nucleosome, across multiple labeling schemes and ATP concentrations. Under the conditions used (without acceptor nucleosomes, DNA, transcription factors, or chaperones), RSC remodels primarily by DNA translocation without lifting DNA by a large distance from the nucleosomal surface. The data are consistent with DNA movement largely along or close to the canonical wrapping path.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C88 accurately summarize the experimental findings from claims C62-C84. The conclusions are well-supported by the extensive data across multiple constructs, ATP concentrations, and labeling schemes. The authors appropriately note the specific experimental conditions.

results.result: Interpretation of DNA path during remodeling: RSC may cause DNA unwrapping or lifting but still hold the DNA near the nucleosome surface. This interpretation is consistent with electron microscopy structures showing tight fit of the nucleosome in RSC's central cavity.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C90 provide reasonable interpretation of the data. The authors appropriately acknowledge that their FRET measurements cannot exclude small-scale DNA lifting or unwrapping if the DNA remains near the surface. The EM structure citation (C90) provides independent support for this interpretation.

results.result: Quantitative analysis of step sizes: The observed ΔFRET step sizes of 0.08-0.11 likely correspond to distance changes of ~0.3-0.6 nm. Based on nucleosome crystal structure geometry, 1 bp translocation should produce ~0.3 nm distance change on average, consistent with a ~1-2 bp step size.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C92 provide quantitative analysis linking FRET changes to physical distances and base pair movements. The calculations are based on established Förster radius values and crystal structure data, making them well-supported. This analysis strengthens the interpretation of step sizes.

results.result: Comparison with SF2 ATPase translocation mechanisms: Some SF2 ATPase-containing DNA translocases/helicases translocate DNA in 1 bp increments. RSC translocates DNA at the SHL2 site where its ATPase domain engages the nucleosome. The isolated RSC catalytic subunit translocates naked DNA in ~2 bp increments. The SF2 ATPase domain of RSC might translocate DNA at the SHL2 site in 1 bp steps.
results.evaluation: Claims C93, C95-C96 cite prior literature appropriately. Claim C94 is speculative but reasonable given the data and prior work on SF2 ATPases. The speculation is appropriately qualified with "might."

results.result: Reinterpretation of previously observed ~50 bp steps: The previously observed ~50 bp translocation steps likely do not reflect the fundamental step size but may be compound steps composed of many ~1-2 bp steps, reflecting relatively long kinetic pauses imposed by the nucleosomal energy landscape.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C98 provide a reasonable reinterpretation of prior literature (C15) in light of the current findings. The interpretation is appropriately qualified as speculative ("may be") and is consistent with the observation of missed steps in the current data.

results.result: Caveats and limitations: RSC and SWI/SNF complexes have somewhat different nucleosome-binding cavities, so they may not translocate DNA identically. Measurements were performed at limiting ATP concentrations (up to ~Km of 80 µM), and behavior might differ at higher concentrations. However, behavior at limiting ATP likely reflects the nucleosome's response to individual translocation events at the SHL2 site.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C103 appropriately acknowledge limitations and caveats. The structural differences between RSC and SWI/SNF (C99) are cited. The ATP concentration limitation (C101) is an important caveat, though the interpretation (C103) is reasonable.

results.result: Mechanistic implications: The observation that RSC moves DNA in ~1-2 bp increments at both entry and exit sites suggests DNA motion across the nucleosome is likely coupled directly to DNA translocation at the SHL2 site by the ATPase domain. If intranucleosomal loops exist, they must be small (1-2 bp) or accumulate/release gradually in 1-2 bp increments, requiring a specific extrusion mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 provide mechanistic interpretation of the findings. The coupling interpretation (C104) is well-supported by the consistency of step sizes at entry and exit sites. The constraints on loop models (C105) are logical consequences of the data, though the authors appropriately note they cannot directly detect loops.

results.result: Comparison with ISWI-family remodelers: The nucleosome translocation step size for RSC is similar to that previously observed for ISWI-family enzymes. For both families, the step sizes likely result from the intrinsic DNA translocation step size of their SF2 ATPase domains. However, SWI/SNF-family remodelers disrupt DNA-octamer contacts more extensively than ISWI-family remodelers. Despite such disruption, RSC likely still holds DNA close to the nucleosome, so disruption does not strongly perturb translocation step sizes.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C109 provide thoughtful comparison with ISWI remodelers. The similarity in step sizes (C106) is supported by citation to prior work (C16). The interpretation that both use similar ATPase mechanisms (C107) is reasonable. The distinction regarding DNA-octamer disruption (C108-C109) is supported by citations and provides important mechanistic insight.

results.result: Core conclusions from abstract: RSC primarily translocates DNA around the nucleosome without substantial H2A-H2B dimer displacement. At entry and exit sites, DNA moves largely along or near its canonical wrapping path. Translocation occurs in a stepwise manner with step size distributions peaking at approximately 1-2 bp at both sites. This suggests DNA movement across the nucleosome is likely coupled directly to DNA translocation by the ATPase at its binding site inside the nucleosome.
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C6 represent the main conclusions stated in the abstract. These are well-supported by the extensive experimental data described in the grouped results above. The conclusions are appropriately qualified ("primarily," "largely," "likely") and represent significant advances in understanding SWI/SNF remodeling mechanisms.
